description: Create Lambda function code, deployment script, and teardown script for persistent B300/H200 spot capacity polling via EventBridge + SNS
steps: Create infra/lambda/capacity_poller/handler.py - Python 3.12 Lambda function that: (a) For each target (p5en.48xlarge and p6-b300.48xlarge) across all configured AZs, attempts a probe run_instances call. (b) If probe succeeds: terminates the probe instance immediately, reads the recipe file content (embedded in the Lambda code as constants since Lambda can't read local files at runtime), renders the env prelude + bootstrap script (same logic as launch-bench-ec2.sh), uploads bootstrap to S3, launches the real benchmark instance with user-data stub that fetches from S3. (c) Publishes SNS notification with instance type, region, AZ, run_id, estimated cost. (d) Disables the EventBridge rule for the successfully-launched instance type. (e) If both types launched, disables all rules. (f) SELF_TERMINATE must be set to 'false' so instances stay alive for debugging. (g) Handles InsufficientInstanceCapacity gracefully (just log and continue).

The Lambda handler must embed: subnet mapping (all 8 AZs), recipe content for both h200 and b300, the full bench-bootstrap.sh content (read at deploy time and embedded as a constant or loaded from a co-packaged file in the zip), security group lookup logic, AMI resolution via SSM.

Create infra/lambda/capacity_poller/bootstrap_embed.py - a helper that packages bench-bootstrap.sh content as a Python constant, OR just include bench-bootstrap.sh in the Lambda zip and read it at runtime.

Create infra/deploy-poller.sh that: (a) Creates SNS topic 'tpot-bench-capacity-alerts'. (b) Creates IAM role 'tpot-bench-poller-lambda-role' with permissions for ec2:RunInstances, ec2:TerminateInstances, ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups, ec2:DescribeInstances, ssm:GetParameter, s3:PutObject, sns:Publish, events:DisableRule, events:DescribeRule, iam:PassRole, logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents. (c) Packages Lambda code into zip (handler.py + bench-bootstrap.sh + recipe files). (d) Creates Lambda function 'tpot-bench-capacity-poller' with 60s timeout, 256MB memory, Python 3.12 runtime. (e) Creates EventBridge rule 'tpot-bench-poll-capacity' with rate(3 minutes). (f) Adds Lambda permission for EventBridge to invoke it. (g) Adds EventBridge target pointing to the Lambda.
Create infra/teardown-poller.sh that removes: EventBridge rule + targets, Lambda function, IAM role + policies, SNS topic. Idempotent (handles 'not found' gracefully).
Include the recipe file contents and bootstrap script in the Lambda package by copying them into the zip at deploy time. The Lambda reads them from its local filesystem (co-packaged files).

Key detail for user-data rendering in Lambda: replicate the S3-stub pattern from launch-bench-ec2.sh. Upload the full rendered bootstrap (env prelude + recipe + bench-bootstrap.sh) to s3://{bucket}/bootstrap/{run_id}/bench-bootstrap.sh, then user-data is just a small stub that downloads and execs it.

Instance launch parameters: 200GB gp3 root, IMDSv2 required, instance-initiated-shutdown-behavior=terminate, spot one-time with terminate on interruption, tags Project=tpot-benchmark + Name=tpot-bench-{type} + RunId={run_id}.

CRITICAL USER REQUIREMENT: Set SELF_TERMINATE='false' in the env prelude so instances do NOT auto-terminate. The user wants to SSH/SSM in to debug if there are problems. Logs are preserved on instance and streamed to S3.
acceptance_criteria: infra/lambda/capacity_poller/handler.py exists and passes Python syntax validation
Lambda handler correctly implements probe-then-launch logic for both instance types
SNS notification is published on successful launch
EventBridge rule is disabled after successful launch for that instance type
SELF_TERMINATE is set to false in rendered user-data
Bootstrap script and recipe files are included in Lambda package
findings: All three files created and verified. Python handler passes AST validation, both shell scripts pass bash -n. SELF_TERMINATE set to false as required. Lambda zip includes co-packaged bench-bootstrap.sh and both recipe files. Deploy script is idempotent (handles existing resources). Teardown uses safe_run pattern for idempotency.
